draft.title: The end of empires
card: An empire is a state that rules over other lands and peoples, often by force. From the late 1800s, European empires such as Britain and France competed to gain more colonies and power.
At the same time, new nation states formed. A nation state is a country whose people share a common identity, such as language or culture, and are ruled by one government.
Italy was unified in 1861 and Germany in 1871. Both joined smaller states into single, stronger countries that could compete with older powers.
Meiji Japan, from 1868, built a modern state with a new army, industry and government. By the early 1900s Japan had also gained colonies of its own.
draft.remember: Old empires and new nation states competed for land and power from the late 1800s.

a.q: What was a new nation state, as formed in Italy and Germany?
opts: A country whose people share an identity and one government
A colony ruled by a distant European empire
A group of states that each kept its own separate government
A territory held by force for another country's army
a.why: Italy and Germany joined many smaller states into one country with a shared identity and one government. A colony is the opposite, because it is ruled by another state.
a.clue: Think of what joined the people of Italy or Germany together.

b.q: Which event shows a new nation state emerging in the late 1800s?
opts: The unification of Germany in 1871
Britain adding new colonies in Africa
France ruling territories in Southeast Asia
Britain and France competing for colonies
b.why: In 1871 Germany became one country under one government, so a nation state emerged. The other three show established empires ruling or competing for overseas land, not a new nation state forming.
b.clue: Look for the option where separate states became one country.

a.best: A country whose people share an identity and one government

b.q: Which of these shows a new nation state forming, rather than an empire growing?
opts: German states joining under one government in 1871
Japan taking Korea as a colony of its own in 1910
Britain claiming new colonies across Africa in the 1880s
France expanding its rule over Indochina in the 1880s
b.why: In 1871 separate German states became one country under one government, so a nation state formed. Japan was a new modern state, but taking Korea meant ruling another people by force, which is empire building, just like Britain in Africa and France in Indochina.
b.clue: Ask whether people are joining together or another people is being ruled.
